citation.title: Process-aware topology optimization leveraging deep learning surrogate model-based functions for laser powder bed fusion
citation.authors: Praveen S. Vulimiri, Shane Garner, Albert C. To
citation.venue: Additive Manufacturing 118 (issue dated February 2026) 105094 (Crossref; published 2026-01-23 per the pool record). Hybrid open access, CC BY-NC, per OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar; Crossref licence metadata includes CC BY-NC 4.0
citation.version_coded: none: only the abstract and highlights were read (pool record from OpenAlex). The version of record (ScienceDirect PII S2214860426000205) could not be retrieved by script

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: Not coded (no accessible full text). Abstract only: a surrogate trained on elastoplastic layerwise inherent-strain FEA drives distortion-aware LPBF topology optimization; the largest case, over 400 iterations, finished in 2.5 days versus 4 days for one verification FEA process simulation.
claim.location: Abstract and highlights (the only text read)
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Not coded (no full text). Would-be values from the abstract and highlights: 4 days ÷ 2.5 days = 1.6 [derived] for the whole surrogate-based optimization against a single FEA process simulation; the surrogate is said to evaluate over 100 times faster than one FEA-based process simulation (highlights).

Pointers from the abstract for the verifier: §5.1 rule 1 would select the abstract's quantitative comparison (the 400-plus-iteration optimization finished in 2.5 days, faster than the 4 days of one verification FEA process simulation), with the highlight's over-100× per-evaluation speed-up of the surrogate against one FEA process simulation as the alternative; both compare against a classical analysis rather than a classical optimizer, so speed stratum only as a cost proxy, as in P00149. The abstract also reports designs with similar mechanical performance, less distortion and zero build failures, verified by simulation and experiment. Physics: elastoplastic residual distortion from the LPBF process coupled with an end-use elastic objective (physics coded 'other', following screening).
